newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Bank Pekao lifts '96 pre-tax to PLN 422 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish Bank Pekao lifts '96 pre-tax to PLN 422 mln.

text.p: Polish state-owned Bank Pekao SA lifted pre-tax profit to 422.4 million zlotys last year from 304.3 million zlotys in 1995, the bank's president said on Friday.
"The year 1996 for was a good one for Bank Pekao SA, as far as our results are concerned...Of course they're preliminary results, not audited," Andrzej Dorosz told a news conference.
Dorosz said net profit shrank to 267.8 million zlotys from 302.2 million zlotys because the bank had been freed from income tax in 1995.
Pekao deputy president Krzysztof Kalicki, also present, said net profit would have grown by 63.8 percent last year if 1995's income tax break had not been granted.
Pekao officials would not give a 1997 forecast though Dorosz said the bank planned to maintain its development growth.
In November Pekao formed a banking group with Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA (PBG), Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy (BDK) Pomorski Bank Kredytowy w Szczecinie SA (PBKS).
Dorosz said the group, whose privatisation is due in 1998, would like to start the sale by placing a small package of shares on the bourse.

He said the combined net profit of the banks in the group rose to 520.8 million zlotys last year from 460.4 million zlotys the year before while pre-tax profit rose to 848.4 million zlotys from 689.4 million.
The group is expected to provide its first consolidated figures next year, with the Arthur Andersen consulting firm advising on the consolidation.
Dorosz said the firms would instal a common computer system and form a common brokerage.

Bank Pekao's own funds increased to 1.1 billion zlotys last year from 737 million in 1995 and its balance sheet total rose to 23.6 billion zlotys from 19.6 billion, the latter growth putting the bank second domestically, Dorosz said.
He said that last year Pekao upped market share in loans to large enterprises to five percent from three percent and lifted its retail market share to five percent from one percent.
